title: Is Atlanta a Good City for Automotive Careers?
summary: As one of the busiest transportation hubs in the Southeast, Atlanta may be a great metro area if you want to build an auto tech car
body_markdown:
As one of the busiest transportation hubs in the Southeast, Atlanta may be a great metro area if you want to build an auto tech career. With millions of daily commuters on major highways like I-75 and I-285, commercial truckers' routes, and a growing population, the city depends heavily on reliable transportation—and[the people with the skills to keep it all moving](https://www.lincolntech.edu/news/automotive/automotive-technology/what-does-auto-mechanic-do-atlanta) .


Whether you already live in the area or are thinking about a move to pursue an auto career, Atlanta provides you access to hands-on skills training programs, as well as opportunities to find work at dealerships, fleet operations, independent repair shops, logistics companies, and specialty automotive businesses that need trained technicians. So, how great of a city is Atlanta for automotive careers? For many aspiring technicians, it can be the key location for a long, successful career.


## Atlanta’s Transportation Industry Drives Automotive Technician Demand


While the need for auto mechanics is steady across the country, demand in Georgia is more than 2X the national average1. Major interstates like I-20, I-75, I-85, and I-285 move thousands of personal and commercial vehicles through the city and surrounding areas every day. That constant movement creates demand for automotive professionals who can keep vehicles operating safely and efficiently. Delivery companies, rideshare drivers, commercial fleets, contractors, and commuters all rely on repair and maintenance services throughout the metro area. That consistent demand creates opportunities across several industries instead of one narrow career path automotive technicians.


## Atlanta Has a Strong Automotive Manufacturing Presence


Atlanta is home to many automotive dealers, manufacturers, and headquarters that drive the vehicle industry forward. Major manufacturers such as[Porsche North America](https://newsroom.porsche.com/en/company/porsche-experience-center-headquarters-atlanta-11000.html) and[Mercedes-Benz](https://group.mercedes-benz.com/careers/about-us/locations/location-detail-page-5206.html) have established headquarters in the Atlanta metro area.[Cox Automotive](https://www.coxautoinc.com/) , which owns and operates other major automotive brands like Cox Fleet, Autotrader, and Kelly Bluebook, also call Atlanta home.[Many of these companies need skilled technicians](https://www.lincolntech.edu/news/automotive/automotive-technology/automotive-mechanic-salary-guide-united-states) for repairs on cars and fleet vehicles, automotive reconditioning, and EV services. As Atlanta continues to grow, so does the need for technicians who can work on both traditional gas-powered vehicles and newer automotive technologies.


## Atlanta Offers Competitive Salaries for Auto Techs


As an automotive technician in the Atlanta metro area, your earning potential may beat out earners in other areas of the country. Atlanta has one of the highest median salaries in Georgia and it also boasts a higher median salary compared to automotive techs around the nation2. Many other factors can affect your potential earnings aside from location, including bonuses and overtime, additional benefits, and pay structure.


## Automotive Tech and Policy Continue to Evolve in Atlanta


Today’s automotive industry looks very different than it did ten years ago. Effective January 1, 2026, the[City of Atlanta mandated electric vehicle infrastructure inclusion for new construction](https://www.100atl.com/electric-vehicles) and major renovations across commercial, multifamily, and residential developments. With these changes, you can expect to see more EVs around the city, which also means there may be a higher need for auto techs skilled in EV maintenance. On top of that, modern vehicles rely heavily on onboard computers, advanced electronics, safety technology, and digital diagnostics.


As an automotive technician in Atlanta, you may work with:


- Computerized engine diagnostics
- Hybrid and EV systems
- Advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS)
- Electronic steering and braking systems
- Vehicle communication networks
- Emissions and fuel efficiency systems


Because of these changes to both vehicles and policy, many employers look for technicians who understand modern automotive technology.


## Atlanta Offers Multiple Types of Automotive Employers


One advantage of building an automotive career in Atlanta is the variety of possible employers throughout the region. If you want dealership experience, you may find opportunities with groups like[Jim Ellis Automotive Group](https://www.jimellis.com/) or[AutoNation](https://www.autonation.com/cars-for-sale/atlanta-ga) locations throughout Metro Atlanta. If fleet maintenance interests you, companies like[Penske Truck Leasing](https://www.pensketruckrental.com/locations/us/georgia/atlanta/) , and regional transportation companies that may employ technicians like[Knight Transportation](https://www.knighttrans.com/locations/atlanta-ga/) . Independent repair facilities and national service chains also hire technicians across the area, including employers like[Pep Boys](https://www.pepboys.com/stores/ga/atlanta) and[Mavis Tires & Brakes](https://www.mavis.com/locations/atlanta-ga/) locations around Atlanta.


## Ready to Start Your Automotive Career in Atlanta?


If you want a hands-on career that combines technology, diagnostics, and real-world problem-solving, Atlanta can offer strong opportunities to begin building your future in automotive technology. And Lincoln Tech can help you get there.[Our Georgia campus Automotive Technology program](https://www.lincolntech.edu/programs/automotive/automotive-technology/georgia) provides hands-on training designed to help you prepare for entry-level automotive careers in the Atlanta area. Fill out the form on the page to learn more about the program and explore your next steps toward becoming an automotive technician in Atlanta.
